name: chown32
synopsis: int chown(const char *pathname, uid_t owner, gid_t group);
int fchown(int fd, uid_t owner, gid_t group);
int lchown(const char *pathname, uid_t owner, gid_t group);
int fchownat(int dirfd, const char *pathname, uid_t owner, gid_t group, int flags);
description: These system calls change the owner and group of a file. They differ in how the file is specified, such as by pathname, file descriptor, or with additional options. Only privileged processes can change the owner, and specific rules apply for group changes.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Path to the file for chown and lchown

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: New owner user ID, or -1 to not change

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: New group ID, or -1 to not change

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bit mask for fchownat, such as AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Search permission is denied on a component of the path prefix
fd is not a valid open file descriptor, or dirfd is invalid for fchownat
pathname points outside accessible address space
Invalid flag specified in flags for fchownat
A low-level I/O error occurred while modifying the inode
Too many symbolic links were encountered in resolving pathname
A component of the path prefix is not a directory, or dirfd is not a directory for fchownat
The calling process did not have the required permissions, or the file is marked immutable
The named file resides on a read-only filesystem

bugs: In some kernel versions, the behavior for root changing ownership of executable files may vary regarding S_ISUID and S_ISGID bits; the 4.4BSD version can only be used by the superuser.
versions: fchown() and lchown() since glibc 2.12 with _POSIX_C_SOURCE >= 200809L; fchownat() since glibc 2.10
